documents.title: BLS Employment Situation — July 2012
documents.date_evidence: Release header: until 8:30 a.m. (EDT) Friday, August 3, 2012
documents.provenance: Official archived release, excerpt verified through web retrieval 2026-10-11; no independent contemporaneous capture claim.
documents.verified_excerpt: Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 163,000 in July, and the unemployment rate was essentially unchanged at 8.3 percent
documents.text: On August 3, 2012, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics initially reported that July payroll employment increased by 163,000 and unemployment was 8.3 percent. These are the figures released then, not subsequently revised estimates.

documents.title: Federal Reserve FOMC statement
documents.provenance: Official dated archival release retrieved 2026-10-11; local source bytes retained; no independent contemporaneous capture claim.
documents.verified_excerpt: economic activity decelerated somewhat over the first half of this year
documents.text: On August 1, 2012, the Federal Reserve described slowing economic activity, slow employment growth, and elevated unemployment. It kept the federal funds target at 0 to 0.25 percent and anticipated exceptionally low rates at least through late 2014. That was its stated expectation in 2012, not a claim about what later occurred.
